title: Mini-episode SDK: transactional toolcalls & bounded-fidelity streaming (PRD sketch)
content:
Context and problem statement:
- Hosted streaming users increasingly demand: lower tail latency, predictable token cost, and transactional tool integrations (e.g., db writes, search calls) that don't require full request rollbacks on client failure.
- Current progressive streaming designs focus on single long-lived sessions: large KV caches, heavyweight resume semantics, and coarse-grained toolcall boundaries. This creates operational friction for mobile/edge clients and high-cost short-turn interactions.

Proposal summary (high level):
- Introduce "mini-episodes": intentionally short-lived streaming segments (50-300 tokens typical) that are first-class units for SDKs and the hosted runtime.
- Each mini-episode has: a bounded fidelity profile, an optional transactional toolcall envelope, and a compact resume token. Episodes can be chained by session id but are independently commit/abort-able.

Goals / success criteria:
- Reduce median and P95 generation latency for short interactive turns by 20-30% for common mobile workflows.
- Lower average KV cache pressure and memory churn across GPUs during bursty small requests.
- Provide a developer ergonomics surface that makes transactional toolcalls easy and safe (idempotency, retries, partial-commit semantics).
- Keep additional billing and telemetry transparent to customers (per-episode token accounting + toolcall op counts).

Design: runtime and protocol primitives (sketch)
1) Episode header (compact JSON frame emitted at episode start)
   - episode_id: short base64 id
   - parent_session: opaque session id (optional)
   - fidelity_profile: one-word tag (low/med/high) controlling sampling length, beam/temperature defaults, model variant hints
   - toolcall_intent: optional brief schema (e.g., {name: "upsert_user", commit_semantics: "two-phase|best-effort"})
   - resume_token_hint: opaque short token if resume is supported

2) Streaming frames within episode
   - partial_text frames (delta chunks)
   - structured frames (typed JSON fragments) for actions/toolcall args
   - soft-commit frames: indicate application-level logical checkpoint (non-committal until toolcall commit)

3) Transactional toolcall envelope
   - begin_toolcall(episode_id, op_id, idempotency_key) -> runtime reserves a tool slot (not a literal DB txn)
   - tool-execute: client calls external service (or we call provider-integrations) using provided args and op_id
   - commit/abort: client issues commit(op_id) or abort(op_id); runtime exposes a graceful timeout auto-abort (configurable).
   - semantics: commit attempts best-effort delivery; for strong guarantees customers should use dedicated capacity + explicit two-phase ops through Redwood Dedicated connectors.

4) Resume + hedging
   - resume tokens small and verifiable (cryptographic MAC + sequence counter) to allow reconstruction of episode context without preserving full KV cache on server side.
   - hedged-mini-episodes: for critical low-latency scenes, clients can spec 1-2 hedges; runtime will route to alternate capacity pools. Budgeted hedging (max extra tokens) prevents cost surprises.

SDK ergonomics (developer-facing patterns)
- High-level API (pseudo-js):
  const ep = client.startEpisode({fidelity: 'low', parent: sessionId})
  ep.on('delta', d => render(d))
  await ep.send('Please summarize the last chat point')
  const {action} = await ep.finish({expectAction: true})
  // transactional toolcall
  const op = await ep.beginToolcall('search-and-upsert', {query, idempotencyKey})
  const res = await runSearchAndUpsert(op.args)
  await ep.commitToolcall(op.opId)

- Ergonomic rules and helpers:
  - Automatic idempotency key generation for ephemeral clients.
  - Lightweight `ep.snapshot()` returns a compact resume token for client caching.
  - `ep.fallback()` config: if commit fails, optionally emit compensating action frames that the client can interpret.
  - Debug helpers: show episode telemetry (latency, hedges, toolcall outcome).

Observability & billing model
- Episode-level metrics: tokens_in, tokens_out, wall_ms, toolcall_count, hedges_used, commit_latency.
- Billing: per-token as usual, additional small op fee per committed toolcall (to account for provider integration cost) — transparent in console.
- Alerts: automatic regression detection on commit failure rate and episode P95 latency.

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0: internal dev SDK + runtime experiment (sprint 1-2) — opt-in flag, record metrics only.
- Phase 1: public SDK beta with limited customers (mobile-first partners) — enable budgeted hedging and best-effort transaction envelope.
- Phase 2: GA with console controls (per-customer defaults for fidelity lanes, hedging budgets, transaction timeouts).

Operational risks and mitigations
- Risk: Developers assume strong ACID semantics for toolcalls.
  - Mitigation: explicit labeling in SDK and docs; provide helper lib for durable two-phase commit through Dedicated or external orchestration.
- Risk: Small episodes may increase per-request overhead (more RPCs).
  - Mitigation: batching heuristics in runtime: coalesce episodes from same client within short window; client-side default to re-use warm channel.
- Risk: Hedging cost blowouts.
  - Mitigation: strict per-episode hedging budgets tied to billing alerts; runtime caps on hedges for free tiers.

Open questions / TODOs (research & UX)
- Tune episode length sweet spot by workload class (conversational vs code generation vs retrieval-assisted). Experiment matrix planned for next sprint.
- Exact schema for structured frames (we should align with typed-tool-contracts work).
- UX flow for commit failures: should we auto-retry toolcalls from runtime or push to client?
- Security: what info is safe to include in resume tokens? consider KMS-bound tokens.

Appendix: short examples and edge cases (notes)
- Edge case: client disconnects after beginToolcall but before commit. Runtime should hold reservation for N seconds, then auto-abort; commit after abort returns deterministic failure code indicating late-commit.
- Example: mobile app uses low-fidelity mini-episodes for autocomplete + quick lookups (search toolcall). If commit fails, app shows cached suggestion and queues compensation write when connection restores.

References and related work: many existing hosted-api drafts explore partial resume and streaming schemas; this is intentionally focused on combining short-lived streaming with transactional tool envelopes and a simple SDK model for mobile/edge ergonomics. See linked Linear ticket and GH PR for prototype client code.

Immediate next steps (for sprint planning):
- Spike: implement episode header + stream frames in dev runtime (owner: Jordan) — 1 week.
- SDK stub: JS + Python startEpisode / beginToolcall / commit APIs (owner: Elliot) — 1 week.
- Lab tests: run microbench matrix (short turns) vs baseline to measure p50/p95 improvements (owner: Maya) — 2 weeks.
- Draft doc for public beta including sample console settings and billing note (owner: Priya) — 1 week.

Notes to self: keep this intentionally lightweight. Aim for pragmatic defaults over configurability at beta. Follow up with infra on KV cache eviction strategies and SRE on hedging resource accounting.
